boundaries: Line 10228 closes C20g's renderTrimPathsGroup; C20h begins at the `// ---- Text Animators — TIMELINE rows (2026-08-31) ----` header on line 10229. Line 10670 closes C20h's renderVertexRow; line 10671 is a trailing blank line; line 10672 opens C20i's `// ---- Motion mode UI: keyframe tracks (mirrors the layer list's rows) ----` header. All four boundary lines confirmed by direct `sed -n` read of the frozen blob.

`fieldParent` has ZERO entries anywhere in src/js/i18n.js (confirmed by grep across all locale blocks), while `fieldBlend` has four (en/fr/ja/es: 'Blend'/'Fondu'/'ブレンド'/'Mezcla'). This scope's own renderDiscreteKeyGridRow (packet 5) takes `label` as a plain parameter and never itself calls SM.t on it, so the asymmetry is entirely in C20i's own call sites (motion.js:11175-11176, cited by line only): `SM.t('fieldParent') || 'Parent'` silently falls back to the hardcoded English literal in every locale including French, while the neighboring Blend row (`SM.t('fieldBlend')`, no fallback) localizes correctly. Not a bug in this scope's own code — recorded here because the issue's own 'Record explicitly' instruction asks which SM.t keys each row emits, and this is the one place a key that should exist does not.

`pathVertexRowCount` (motion.js:4598-4600, out of this scope, cited by line only) has NO cap — it returns `sd.centerSegments.length` for a vector-brush ribbon or `sd.segments.length` for an ordinary path, unbounded. `meshVertexRowCount` (motion.js:4796-4802, out of this scope, cited by line only) explicitly caps at `MESH_ROW_CAP=200` (motion.js:4796). This scope's own renderPathVertexGroup/renderPathGroupTrackRow (packet 4) and renderMeshVertexGroup/renderVertexRow (packet 6) both simply loop `for (var vi=0; vi<vertexCount; vi++)` over whatever `vertexCount` their caller passes — neither packet enforces the cap itself; the asymmetry (a path can produce arbitrarily many rows, a mesh cannot exceed 200) lives entirely in the two upstream row-count functions, not in this scope's own rendering loops.

`ensureElementHolder(ld, key)` (motion.js:2879-2907, out of this scope, cited by line only) and the read-only `meshHolder(li, meshId)` (motion.js:4747-4750, out of this scope, cited by line only) both resolve into the SAME flat `ld.elementMotion` object, keyed by whatever string is passed — a per-shape `strokeId` for an ordinary element holder, or a `meshId` for a mesh holder (video-level or per-element). This scope's own renderPathVertexGroup/renderMeshVertexGroup never construct a holder themselves; they receive an already-resolved holder object from their caller (C20g's renderElementsList at motion.js:9955/9964, this file's own right-panel mirror at motion.js:7628/7631/7509, and C20i's renderTimelineMotion at motion.js:11282/11294) and are agnostic to which key namespace produced it. Nothing in the observed code enforces that a strokeId and a meshId can never collide as object keys of the same `ld.elementMotion` map; no collision was found or is claimed, this is a structural observation about a shared namespace, not a reported bug.

`ld.textAnimators[i]` entries are holders in their own right — `renderTextAnimatorsList` (packet 1) passes `an` directly wherever this scope's own TA_TIMELINE_FIELDS.forEach hands it to `renderTrimScalarRow(list, an, f.prop, ...)` (motion.js:10292-10294, C20g), and the grid mirror does the same via `TA_TIMELINE_FIELDS.forEach(function (f) { renderTracksFor(grid, an, f.prop); })` (motion.js:11370, C20i). There is no `ensureElementHolder`-style lazy allocator for a text animator's own `.motion`/`.motionStatic` fields visible in this scope; their initial allocation (if any) happens wherever `ld.textAnimators` entries are first created, outside this scope's own read-only line range.

`keyWholePath`/`unkeyWholePath`/`pathGroupKeysAt` (packet 3) never call `pushUndo` themselves. The ONLY reachable UI path to either is renderPathVertexGroup's own group-stopwatch click handler (packet 4, motion.js:10386: `e.stopPropagation(); pushUndo();` immediately before branching to `unkeyWholePath`/`keyWholePath` at motion.js:10387-10388) and renderPathGroupTrackRow's own diamond mousedown handler (packet 4, motion.js:10428: `pushUndo();` before calling `pathGroupKeysAt` again post-`goToFrame` at motion.js:10430-10431 and setting up the group drag). Both call sites for these three helpers are inside this SAME leaf (packet 4), so no external caller was found or is possible to exist yet (see reconciliation for the confirmed zero-external-caller grep result) — but if a future caller invoked any of the three directly without its own pushUndo, the write would happen without history capture; nothing in the three functions themselves guards against that.

renderDiscreteKeyGridRow's (packet 5) three DOCUMENT-write paths are: (1) plain click on an unselected key when nothing is selected — `setKeySel([{holder,prop,key:k}])` (motion.js:10548) plus a fresh single-key `window._motionKeyDrag` (motion.js:10560-10562), pushUndo already called at motion.js:10554 just above the branch; (2) plain click on an already-selected key — reuses the WHOLE `_motionKeySel` array for the group drag (motion.js:10567-10570), same pushUndo at 10554; (3) right-click delete — the context menu action (motion.js:10578-10586) calls `pushUndo()` (motion.js:10580) then the caller-supplied `removeAt(frame)` (motion.js:10581, which for Parent/Blend rows resolves to `SMMotion.removeParentKeyAt`/`SMMotion.removeBlendKeyAt`, C20i's own call sites at motion.js:11175-11176, bodies out of this scope), then `setKeySel(...)` to drop the deleted key from the live selection (motion.js:10582) and the paired renderLayerList/renderTimeline plus a guarded SMEngineBridge.renderNow (motion.js:10583-10584). Cmd/Ctrl-click (motion.js:10515-10523) and Shift-click (motion.js:10527-10552) toggle/extend `_motionKeySel` without pushUndo or removeAt — pure selection, no document write.

Confirmed via grep across app.js and engine-bridge.js: none of the twelve span symbols (TA_TIMELINE_FIELDS, isTextAnimatorExpanded, renderTextAnimatorsList, isPathGroupExpanded, pathGroupFrames, pathGroupKeysAt, keyWholePath, unkeyWholePath, renderPathVertexGroup, renderPathGroupTrackRow, renderDiscreteKeyGridRow, renderMeshVertexGroup, renderVertexRow) are referenced by getEffectiveStrokes/getEffectiveStrokesRendered (app.js:2949/1796) or buildSceneJson (engine-bridge.js:772) — this span is Motion timeline UI only, never on the render/export path.

packets.signature: renderDiscreteKeyGridRow(grid, holder, prop, label, keys, removeAt) -> undefined
packets.responsibility: Lead-in (10451-10481, 31 lines, two feedback items): first (#207/#214) states WHY Blend/Parent need a generic discrete (hold-only) grid row — a plain [{frame,...}] array with no interpolation, so selection/drag/delete reuse setKeySel/_motionKeySel/isKeySelected and the shared window._motionKeyDrag group-drag object rather than trackRowHtml's full numeric-track pipeline (ease boxes, hold/linear menu, skew-drag — none apply to a discrete track); the ONE piece that makes all of that generic machinery work unmodified is trackFor's own extension to resolve 'blendKeys'/'parentKeys' (already present at motion.js:454-455, this scope only relies on it).
